items.title: Phase 0 shell substrate
items.decision: Use Vite, TypeScript, native DOM, and native IndexedDB for the initial foundation.
items.why: Minimizes runtime dependencies and duplicate authority while keeping the public contracts replaceable.
items.revisitWhen: After exact-source NeumanOS/Kurumi characterization and schema-driven UI bake-off.

items.title: Whole-application launchpad route
items.decision: Keep the small Omnevum Vite/TypeScript/native-DOM foundation as the launchpad; harvest NeumanOS and Kurumi patterns in isolated qualification work rather than adopting either whole application.
items.why: Both candidates have high feature and test value, but importing either would introduce a second application authority, framework-specific route/store ownership, and lifecycle surface before Omnevum contracts are proven.
items.revisitWhen: A representative benchmark proves an exact candidate can satisfy Omnevum canonical ownership, static-host, accessibility, migration, security, and replacement gates with lower total lifecycle cost.

items.title: Vault and sync candidate route
items.decision: Retain the native small Vault path for Phase 0 and qualify SelfStore as the leading Phase 2 encrypted backup/replica candidate; qualify remoteStorage.js only as an optional endpoint adapter.
items.why: SelfStore has the strongest portable archive, crypto, target, merge, Recovery, and test seams; remoteStorage.js adds a useful open endpoint protocol but requires external service/auth/CORS and cannot be the static-core dependency.
items.revisitWhen: Contract, security, quota, crash, migration, provider, and cross-origin tests pass on representative Vault fixtures.
